I think the solution is to use your function like this:
JavaScript:
var bitmap = ImageManager.loadAchievement(...);
bitmap.addLoadListener(() => this.refresh());
Or something along those lines – basically, make it force a refresh of your window once the image has finished loading.
The other alternative might be to use the
ImageManager.reserveBitmap
function. I don't know exactly how that's meant to be used though. I
think
you'd call it in your scene setup function for every image you need to load, but I'm not sure if you need to do some cleanup when the scene ends or what you should choose as a reservation ID.

That's not really enough information for me to guess what's going on. The code I wrote isn't even valid code (you have to substitute the
...
with the correct parameters, which it sounds like you did).
My code was written under the assumption that you are in a function on some Window_XXX class. So, the full code would be something like this (but the below code uses non-existent names as an example, so it's not copy-pastable):
JavaScript:
Window_Achievement.prototype.something = function() {
    var bitmap = ImageManager.loadAchievement(...);
    bitmap.addLoadListener(() => this.refresh());
    // do other stuff with bitmap, like drawing it or whatever
};
If you pasted it into a different function, it's not guaranteed to work as-is. If you pasted it into a Scene_XXX.prototype.xyz function, replacing
this.refresh()
with
this._someWindow.refresh()
probably gets the same effect.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
The quickest way to add something to the save file is to put it in the
$gameSystem
variable. You could also override
DataManager.makeSaveContents
and
DataManager.extractSaveContents
.
